articles.title: Trump, AI Company Heads Sign White House Accord on Four Safety Checks
articles.description: US President Donald Trump and top technology leaders of Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, Nvidia, and SpaceX signed a voluntary accord that will affect the governance and development of artificial intelligence. The voluntary accord commits each company to follow four stringent layers of controls and audits for its frontier AI models. The high-profile signing of the accord took place on Tuesday, September 29, at the White House Lunch in Washington. The move comes at a time when the rise of AI-related security breaches has been rampant and created doubts about AI safety and regulations . The signatories involved in the accord will use internal controls, an internal team, an outside auditor, and board-level oversight. What Do the Four Layers Include? First, companies must monitor their models during training and use, with a focus on cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical threats. Models must not hack or reach technical systems in unintended ways. Second, an internal team checks that the controls work and fixes any issues. Third, an independent auditor tests the same controls. Fourth, a board-level group reviews the findings. Signatories will also meet twice a year to share progress. Trump described the deal as "almost like a constitution." Asked if it was binding, he said it was "morally" so. The accord itself sets no penalties and has no government enforcement. Experts are not fully convinced. Robin Jia of the University of Southern California questioned how far companies can be trusted to police themselves. Alex Pascal of the Berkman Klein Center called the language broad and vague. He said stronger liability rules would be needed. What Else Should You Know? The accord says these steps could be written into law over time. It also uses the term superintelligence instead of AI, and a new executive order asks federal agencies to follow that wording. Recent events add weight to the debate. In July, OpenAI's agents breached systems at Hugging Face, according to OpenAI's own technical report. Medianama notes the accord would not have forced OpenAI to report that breach any sooner. Europe, in contrast, has chosen binding AI laws.

articles.title: KPMG affirms economic value offered by Falco's Horne 5 project in Québec
articles.description: Professional services firm KPMG finds in a socioeconomic impact study on TSX-V-listed Falco Resources' Horne 5 project that it can contribute $8.8-billion to Québec's GDP over its lifetime. KPMG was appointed to determine the significant economic and labour opportunities offered by the development of the Horne 5 copper and gold project, based on the project's updated feasibility report that was published in July.
